item.title: Juneau Assembly OKs more than $2M toward affordable housing projects
item.description: The projects approved Monday are expected to create more than 40 housing units, including both single-family homes and apartment complexes located throughout the borough.

item.description: Watch Gavel Alaska coverage of Alaska Chief Justice Susan Carney's address.

item.title: Hoffman says ‘it’s time’ as he prepares to wrap up 40-year career in state politics
item.description: Bethel Democratic Sen. Lyman Hoffman recently visited his hometown, where he says he plans to spend some quality time after doing what he can to help fund the state's ailing budget in his final legislative session.

item.title: Washington and other Democratic-led states drop lawsuit against Arctic Refuge oil drilling in Alaska
item.description: A group of environmental and tribal groups had filed suit in 2020 at the same time as the Democratic-led states. Last month, that coalition renewed their suit.

item.title: Alaska school maintenance backlog has reached a crisis, students and school boards tell lawmakers
item.description: Lawmakers with the bipartisan majority caucus have expressed support for more funding for schools, but point to Gov. Dunleavy’s history of vetoes as a major roadblock.

item.title: 3 more families sue Bering Air a year after a deadly crash near Nome
item.description: All of the lawsuits cite the initial finding that the plane flew into icing conditions while overweight.

item.title: Juneau School Board returns $1.05 million in child care funding to city
item.description: The school board unanimously approved returning the funds following multiple delays since November as board members mulled over the future of after-school child care in the district.

item.title: Juneau legislator’s bill banning masked law enforcement faces skepticism from some lawmakers
item.description: Juneau Rep. Sara Hannan says her bill aims to increase police transparency and communication in Alaska.
